exercise.name: Dumbbell Elevated Heel Goblet Squat
aliases: Goblet squat on a slant board

reference.title: Dumbbell Elevated Heel Goblet Squat
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked from this environment); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching

equipment: Low board or plates under the heels

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the top, lower; breathe out as you pass the hardest part of the rise.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, short pause, about 1.2 s up

prescription.progression: Heavier dumbbell, a 2 s pause at the bottom, then a heels-elevated front squat. Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8) at the end of each set.

cues.text: Heels on a low board, balls of the feet on the floor, feet a little narrower than shoulder width. Hold one dumbbell upright against the chest, hands cupping the top plate, elbows down.
Breathe in, brace and sit straight down; let the knees travel forward over the toes, chest tall.
Thighs below parallel, trunk upright, heels pressed into the board.
Drive up through the whole foot and stand tall; breathe out near the top.
Stand tall, reset the brace, repeat.

mistakes.fix: Set the board under the heels only; the balls of the feet stay on the floor.
Keep the knees tracking over the second toe as they travel forward.
The raised heels are there so you can stay upright: keep the dumbbell on the sternum and the chest tall.
Control the descent and pause briefly before driving up.

kinematics.norm: About hip to shoulder width, toes slightly out (common coaching)

About 2-5 cm under the heels (a plate or slant board; common coaching). Raising the heels lets the knees travel further forward for the same ankle range, so the trunk stays more upright and the knee bends deeper (common coaching; clinical opinion)
About 120-135 degrees in a deep heel-raised squat (clinical opinion); depth is driven mostly by knee range (Zawadka 2020)
Not specified by the sources for this depth
More upright than a flat-footed squat; more lean moves demand from knee to hip (Straub 2024)
Held upright at the sternum, elbows down (common coaching)
About 2 s down, about 1 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #23086, Dumbbell Elevated Heel Goblet Squat, video (movement reference)

Collins, Klawitter, Waldera, Mahoney & Christensen 2021, differences in muscle activity and kinetics between the goblet squat and landmine squat in men and women (J Strength Cond Res 35(10):2661-2668)
A biomechanical comparison of back and front squats in healthy trained individuals (J Strength Cond Res 23(1):284-292, 2009; PubMed 19002072)
Zawadka et al. 2020, How are squat timing and kinematics in the sagittal plane related to squat depth? (J Sports Sci Med 19:500-507)
Straub and Powers 2024, a biomechanical review of the squat exercise: implications for clinical practice (Int J Sports Phys Ther)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Choose a dumbbell load you can control for every rep; the load is user-chosen.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knee pain: squat to a shallower depth or lower the board.
Feeling unstable: use a wider board so the whole heel is supported.
regressions: Goblet squat with the feet flat.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Knee extensors lower and drive the squat; the raised heels let the knees travel forward and bend deeper, shifting work toward the quadriceps (clinical opinion). Quadriceps activity was higher in the goblet squat than in the landmine squat (Collins 2021).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Knee extensors lower and drive the squat; the raised heels let the knees travel forward and bend deeper, shifting work toward the quadriceps (clinical opinion). Quadriceps activity was higher in the goblet squat than in the landmine squat (Collins 2021).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Hip extensor, working hardest out of the bottom (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Hip extensor, working hardest out of the bottom (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus assists hip extension in the deep squat; the knees pushing out keeps the thighs over the feet (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus assists hip extension in the deep squat; the knees pushing out keeps the thighs over the feet (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Co-contract around the knee and assist hip extension (Collins 2021 measured biceps femoris and semitendinosus in both squats).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Co-contract around the knee and assist hip extension (Collins 2021 measured biceps femoris and semitendinosus in both squats).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Steady the shins as the knees travel forward over the toes.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Steady the shins as the knees travel forward over the toes.
muscleNotes.core: Braces against the load held in front of the body.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the chest up and the back flat under the front load (clinical opinion). A front-loaded squat needed less knee compression than a back squat for similar muscle recruitment (front vs back squat, 2009).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the chest up and the back flat under the front load (clinical opinion). A front-loaded squat needed less knee compression than a back squat for similar muscle recruitment (front vs back squat, 2009).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the knees tracking over the toes (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the knees tracking over the toes (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Cup the top plate and keep the dumbbell from slipping (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Cup the top plate and keep the dumbbell from slipping (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Hold the elbows bent and the dumbbell against the chest (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Hold the elbows bent and the dumbbell against the chest (clinical opinion).
